package_info.package_versions: All unpatched versions prior to April and July 2023 security updates (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The MSMQ service contains multiple critical vulnerabilities in its message header parsing routines, allowing remote attackers to trigger out-of-bounds reads and writes via crafted network packets. These flaws enable remote code execution and denial-of-service attacks, making the service dangerous in its unpatched state.

execution_context.trigger: network packet parsing (runtime, upon receiving a crafted MSMQ packet)
execution_context.file_location: MQQM.DLL (user-mode MSMQ message header parser, function CQmPacket::CQmPacket)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a crafted MSMQ packet is received, the code reads StreamIdSize and OrderQueueSize fields from the EodHeader without validating their values, leading to an out-of-bounds read and potential denial-of-service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fails to validate attacker-controlled size fields before memory access, allowing out-of-bounds reads that can crash the service.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal MSMQ packet parsing should strictly validate all header sizes to prevent memory access violations. Here, the parser trusts untrusted network data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code may copy variable-length fields, but only after strict bounds checking.
key_indicators: Lack of bounds checking on network-supplied size fields
Direct memory access based on untrusted input

execution_context.trigger: network packet parsing (runtime, upon receiving a crafted MSMQ packet)
execution_context.file_location: MQQM.DLL (user-mode MSMQ message header parser, function CQmPacket::CQmPacket)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a crafted MSMQ packet is received, the code uses an attacker-controlled size field from various message headers (EodHeader, EodAckHeader, CompoundMessageHeader) to perform memory writes without proper validation, leading to out-of-bounds write and potential remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows arbitrary memory writes based on untrusted network data, enabling attackers to corrupt memory and potentially execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior requires strict validation of all size fields before memory operations. Here, the parser fails to enforce this.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Variable-length data is common in protocol parsing, but always with strict validation.
key_indicators: No upper bound or sanity check on header size

execution_context.trigger: network packet parsing (runtime, upon receiving a crafted MSMQ packet with CompoundMessageHeader and SecurityHeader)
execution_context.file_location: MQAC.SYS (kernel-mode MSMQ component, function CQmPacket::GetPacketBody and related functions)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a crafted MSMQ packet with a malformed CompoundMessageHeader is received, the code uses the MsgBodySize field without validation to perform a memory write in kernel space, leading to an out-of-bounds write and potential remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows an attacker to control the size of a memory write in kernel space, which can be exploited for privilege escalation or remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Kernel code must strictly validate all untrusted input, especially size fields from network packets. Here, the parser fails to do so.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate kernel code may copy message bodies, but only after strict validation.
key_indicators: No validation of attacker-controlled size in kernel memory operation
Direct use of network-supplied size in memcpy

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted MSMQ packet to the target's TCP port 1801.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggering of vulnerable message header parsing routines.

attack_chain.action: MSMQ service parses the malicious packet and processes message headers without proper validation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Out-of-bounds memory access (read or write) in user-mode or kernel-mode components.

attack_chain.action: Out-of-bounds read causes denial-of-service (service crash); out-of-bounds write enables remote code execution or further memory corruption.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial-of-service or full remote code execution on the target system.

behavioral_signatures: MSMQ service crash or abnormal termination after receiving network packets
Unusual memory access violations in MSMQ components (MQQM.DLL, MQAC.SYS)
Inbound traffic to TCP port 1801 with malformed or oversized message headers
file_indicators: Crash dumps or logs referencing CQmPacket::CQmPacket, CQmPacket::GetPacketBody, or related MSMQ parsing functions
Abnormal service restart events for MQSVC.EXE
network_indicators: Inbound MSMQ packets with oversized or malformed EodHeader, EodAckHeader, or CompoundMessageHeader fields
Unusual or repeated connections to TCP port 1801 from untrusted sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor MSMQ service (MQSVC.EXE) for crashes or abnormal restarts, and inspect network traffic to TCP port 1801 for packets with abnormally large or malformed message headers (especially EodHeader, EodAckHeader, CompoundMessageHeader). Use IPS signatures targeting these vulnerabilities (e.g., MS.Windows.MSMQ.CVE-2023-21554.Remote.Code.Execution) and analyze crash dumps for out-of-bounds memory access in MSMQ parsing routines.
